newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: PACKER BIDS FOR SYDNEY HARBOUR CASINO
Media owner Kerry Packer has made a bid to buy the controlling interest in the Sydney Harbour Casino.
New South Wales Gaming Minister, Richard Face, says an announcement by the U-S owners Showboat, and Mr Packer's company PBL, will be made this morning.
Mr Face says the bid requires approval by a number of organisations as well as the Casino Control Authority.
He says there'll be probity checks of the organisations and individuals involved and those checks will be thorough.
If the bid is successful, Mr Packer will have a controlling interest in the two biggest casinos in the country.
He's already the biggest individual investor in Melbourne's Crown Casino.
BIG WELCOME AWAITS RESCUED SAILORS
The scene is set for a rousing welcome at the Port of Fremantle this morning for HMAS Adelaide.
The frigate is carrying two solo yachtsmen and crew who rescued them in treacherous conditions in the Southern Ocean after their yachts capsized.
Briton Tony Bullimore, Frenchman Thierry Dubois and the frigate's crew will be greeted by thousands of people, Defence chiefs, politicians and a huge international media contingent.
A large flotilla of pleasure craft is expected to follow HMAS Adelaide into Fremantle harbour.
The yachtsmen and crew are expected to hold a media conference to describe their ordeal before the sailors undergo medical treatment.
GREEN CORPS TO BE ANNOUNCED THIS MORNING
Federal Environment Minister Robert Hill will this morning announce details the Government's environmental labour force -- the Green Corps.

Senator Hill will announce details the Green Corp's first 24 projects, which will take place in areas such as Shark Bay in Western Australia, Kangaroo Island, the Western Plains Zoo in Dubbo, and Elsey National Park in the Territory.
The initial schemes will employ around 240 young Australians, who'll do work that includes protecting native vegetation, restoring heritage buildings and monitoring water quality.
Each member will be paid up to 246 dollars a week.
ATSIC BOARD MEMBER SAYS QLD GOVT SCAREMONGERING
The states are still grappling with the implications of the High Court's Wik decision, as Aboriginal leaders raise concerns about interpretations of the ruling.
ATSIC board member Geoff Clark says many people are predicting dire results without having read the judgement, and he's singled out Queensland as a scaremonger.
The Queensland Government says it will only issue mining leases over freehold land, until the Wik decision is clarified.
In the Northern Territory, Chief Minister Shane Stone says his Government's considering its options in relation to mining.
CAPE YORK RESIDENTS TO PROTEST OVER WIK
Residents from Cape York Peninsula are organising a protest over the Wik High Court decision, with a mail out to around a thousand people beginning today in the hope of gaining more support.
Residents are planning a convoy to drive to Canberra to deliver a protest message to the Federal Government.
Grazier Graham Elms, from Butchers Hill Homestead, at Lakeland, says more than a dozen residents from the Cape York Land Defenders met yesterday and decided to set up a fighting fund.
Mr Elms says the residents are concerned the Government is going soft, and they want the Government to either legislate or call a referendum.
1996 A HOT YEAR
The Bureau of Meteorology says the average temperature over Australia during 1996 was the fifth highest on record.
The Bureau's Dr Doug Gauntlett says the average temperature was 0.56 degrees above that for 1910 to 1996.
Dr Gauntlett says recent years have been exceptionally warm, with more than half of the top 20 warmest years since 1910 coming in the late 1980s, and the 1990s.
He says a trend in Australia and throughout much of the world has been for overnight minimum temperatures to have increased more than daytime maximum temperatures.
CORPORAL PUNISHMENT IN NSW NON-GOVERNMENT SCHOOLS
In New South Wales, a group of Christian lawyers and parents are considering taking legal action to stop the State Government banning corporal punishment in non-Government schools.
The Religious Freedom Institute, a fledgling group representing some Christian schools and parents, says the legislation is an infringement on private schools' rights.
The ban on corporal punishment, already in place in Government-run schools, will be extended to all schools at the start of term next month.
The Institute has instructed lawyers to investigate ways to stop the law taking effect, and may move to fight the law in court.
